FOREWORD Background of Preparation

To deeply implement CCCC Group's "Internationalization Deepening Reform Plan", solidly advance the Group's overall deployment of constructing a "One Country, One Policy" QHSE management system, and fully promote the Group's overseas QHSE management effectiveness towards leading international standards, the Group's Safety Supervision Department, in 2023, initiated the "Overseas QHSE System Pilot Construction" work. The revision, issuance, and trial implementation of the "Safety and Health Management System" for the CCCC Group Tanzania Country Organization marks a milestone in the Group's "One Country, One Policy" QHSE management system construction. The compilation of the "Safety and Health Management System" for the Tanzania Country Organization is based on documents such as the "CCCC Group and China Communications Construction Company Safety Production Management System Compilation", combined with the "China Communications Construction Company Limited Tanzania Occupational Health and Safety Management System Benchmarking Analysis Report" to determine the compilation direction, and was commissioned to a third-party consulting agency for its preparation. It aims to integrate the complete and advanced ISO 45001 management requirements and measures into the management system currently operating in Tanzania, ultimately forming a complete set of system documents that can effectively guide all CCCC Group projects in Tanzania in
safety and health management.
Success Factors

The purpose of an Occupational Health and Safety Management System (hereinafter referred to as OHSMS) is to provide a framework for managing OH&S risks and opportunities. The aim and intended outcomes are to prevent work-related injury and ill health to workers, provide safe and healthy workplaces, improve OH&S performance, and meet legal requirements and other requirements. However, to ensure the effectiveness of the OHSMS and its ability to achieve its intended outcomes, the implementation of the following factors is critical:
Top management leadership, commitment, responsibilities and accountability of the Country Organization;
The Country Organization's top management developing, leading and promoting a culture in the organization that supports the intended outcomes of the OH&S management system;
Effective internal and external communication;
Consultation and participation of workers, and, where they exist, workers' representatives;
Allocation of the necessary resources to maintain the OHSMS;
OH&S policies and objectives that are compatible with the strategic objectives and direction of the organization;
Effective process(es) for identifying hazards, controlling OH&S risks and taking advantage of OH&S opportunities;
Continual performance evaluation and monitoring of the OH&S management system to improve OH&S performance;
Integration of the OH&S management system into the Country
Organization's daily business processes;
Compliance with its legal requirements and other requirements.

1. Introduction
1.1 Purpose

To establish an Occupational Health and Safety Management System (OHSMS) to effectively manage occupational health and safety in its business activities. By implementing this OHSMS, the aim is to eliminate or minimize OHS risks associated with the company's business activities and to comply with legal and other relevant requirements.
This OHS Manual shall:
Define the OHS policy;
Describe the core elements of the OHS management system;
Specify the supporting procedures;
Ensure continual improvement of OHS performance.
1.2 Scope

This manual, including all related operational procedures and supporting documents, is applicable to the health and safety management activities of all member units of the CCCC Group Tanzania Country Organization.

This manual, including all related operational procedures and supporting documents, is applicable to the occupational health and safety management activities of all projects of the CCCC Group Tanzania Country Organization. Its business activities cover: civil engineering; marine engineering; building and foundation; urban integrated development; pipeline engineering; green power; maintenance engineering; design and operation, and other types of construction projects.
This manual, including all related operational procedures and supporting documents, is applicable to all contractors of the CCCC Group Tanzania Country Organization's projects.
1.3 Establishment, Modification, and Abolition

The Occupational Health and Safety Management System's "Occupational Health and Safety Management Manual (OHSMM)" is prepared by the Tanzania Country Organization and takes effect after approval by the Country Top Management. The "Occupational Health and Safety Management Manual (OHSMM)" is divided into "Controlled" and "Uncontrolled" copies. Its issuance, modification, and abolition shall be approved by the Country Organization's Top Management, and implemented in accordance with OHSPS-PA-012 "Document and Record Management Procedure".
1.4 Normative References

The preparation of this manual references: (1) ISO 45001:2018 Occupational health and safety management systems - Requirements with guidance for use (2) ISO 19011:2018 Guidelines for auditing management systems (3) CCCC Group and China Communications Construction Company Safety Production Management System Compilation 2025 (4) Tanzania local laws and regulations
1.5 Terms and Definitions

This manual quotes the relevant terms and definitions from ISO 45001:2018 "Occupational health and safety management systems Requirements with guidance for use". The main core terms and definitions are as follows:
1.5.1Industry Terms (Applicable for use within CCCC Group and between countries)
ompany: China Communications Construction Company Limited
Country: Refers to the general term for a state widely recognized internationally as having independent sovereignty

Country Organization: China Communications Construction Company Limited Tanzania Country Organization is a flexible organization led by China Harbour as the country-leading unit and co-constructed by main country-level business participating units. It is a small platform for overall country-level management, undertaking functions such as country market coordination, business synergy, resource sharing, compliance
supervision, and work coordination.
Project Department: Refers to the resident institutions and affiliated projects established in Tanzania by units belonging to China Communications Construction Company Limited.

Top Management: The first person in charge of the project appointed by China Communications Construction Company Limited or the highest person in charge of each member unit of the Country Organization.
1.5.2 Standard Terms (ISO 45001 Professional Terms)
OH&S: Occupational Health and Safety
OHSMS: Occupational Health and Safety Management System
For other terms, see Appendix 3: Terms
1.6 OHS Management System Approach

The OH&S management system approach applied in this manual is founded on the concept of Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA). The PDCA concept is an iterative process used by organizations to achieve continual improvement. It can be applied to a management system and to each of its individual elements, as follows:

-Plan (P): determine and assess OH&S risks, OH&S opportunities and other risks and other opportunities, establish OH&S objectives and processes necessary to deliver results in accordance with the organization's OH&S policy.
-Do (D): implement the processes as planned.
-Check (C): monitor and measure activities and processes with regard to the OH&S policy and OH&S objectives, and report the results.
-Act (A): take actions to continually improve the OH&S performance to achieve the intended outcomes.
ISO 45001 incorporates the PDCA concept into a new framework, as shown in Figure 1.

2. Occupational Health and Safety Policy Statement

The Top Management of China Communications Construction Company Limited Tanzania Country Organization establishes, implements, and maintains this policy statement, which declares the commitment to ensure all activities and operations are conducted safely, causing minimal harm to workers, the environment, and the public. To achieve this goal, the Country Organization has established an Occupational Health and Safety Management System in accordance with the ISO 45001:2018 standard, documented in detail in the "Occupational Health
and Safety Management Manual (OHSMM)" to provide guidance for employees.

The objectives of these procedures are to: 1. Prevent accidents; 2. Provide safe and healthy working conditions for the prevention of work-related injury and ill health; 3. Eliminate hazards and reduce OH&S risks; 4. Comply with country-specific local regulations and other relevant requirements; 5. Maintain a high standard of safety at the company's sites; 6. Provide training to employees to enable them to achieve the company's health and safety objectives; 7. Set objectives for achievement and improvement; 8. Monitor and measure the effectiveness of the OHS management system; 9. Commit to consultation and participation of workers;

10. Provide sufficient resources and priority for the implementation of this policy; 11. Occupational health and safety is the primary responsibility of every employee; 12. All employees shall ensure this policy is understood, implemented, and maintained. As an integral part of the company's continual improvement objectives, this policy will be reviewed annually and updated as necessary. Occupational health and safety is the first priority of every employee. All As an inseparable part of the company's objectives, it shall be continually

3.2 Understanding the OHS Policy

This policy is an extension based on the OHS policy of CCCC Group. "People-oriented, Life First, Creating a Safe and Green Work Environment" clarifies the core OHS values and vision of the Tanzania Country. "Integrated Prevention, Full Participation, Continually Reducing and Eliminating Safety Risks" is the methodology, answering "how to do it" and "how to achieve" the above goals, emphasizing dynamic management and continual improvement. It reflects the core concepts and implementation paths of the Tanzania Country in OHS, forming a complete ideological system:
Values: Human life and safety are paramount.
Vision: To create a workplace that is both safe and environmentally friendly.
Method: Adopt systematic and comprehensive prevention strategies, relying on the joint efforts of all employees.
Commitment: Never be satisfied with the status quo, committed to continual improvement, and pursuing excellent safety performance.
3.2.1"People-oriented, Life First"

Clarifies the core OHS value and ultimate goal of the Tanzania Country, and the "highest principle" of safety management. In all production and operation activities, human life, health, and well-being are the highest values, an insurmountable red line.
3.2.2"Creating a Safe and Green Work Environment"

This is the concrete materialization of the "Life First" concept. "Safe" refers to eliminating or controlling risks in the workplace that could cause injury or illness, ensuring the physical and mental health of employees. "Green" emphasizes environmentally friendly sustainable development, minimizing the negative impact of production and operation activities on the environment, and creating a healthy, clean, and sustainable work and living environment for employees and society. It reflects the social responsibility of the Tanzania Country Organization.
3.2.3"Integrated Prevention"

Refers to adopting multi-level, multi-dimensional comprehensive prevention measures, reflecting the core idea of modern safety management. "Integrated Prevention" means the combination of human, technical, and managerial prevention measures to build a tight safety net. Specifically reflected in: (1) Engineering and Technical Measures: Controlling risks at the source through inherently safe design of equipment, technical transformation, isolation, alarm devices, and other hardware. (2) Management and Process Measures: Establishing sound safety management systems, operating procedures, emergency plans, training systems, etc. (3) Behavioral and Cultural Measures: Guiding employees to form safe work habits through education, supervision, and incentives.
3.2.4"Full Participation"

Clarifies that safety is not just the responsibility of the safety management department, but the shared responsibility of everyone from top management to every front-line employee. Specifically reflected in:
Leadership Commitment:
Management must provide resources, lead by example, and demonstrate a firm commitment to safety.

Employee Empowerment: Every employee has the right to refuse unsafe work, the obligation to participate in risk identification, and the responsibility to propose safety improvements. It requires establishing open communication channels and encouraging employees to report hazards and unsafe conditions.
3.2.5"Continually Reducing and Eliminating Safety Risks"

Reflects the endless, continual improvement and dynamic process and commitment of OHS. It promises to continuously identify, assess, and control risks through systematic efforts, pursuing the excellent goal of "zero accidents, zero injuries, zero pollution". It is reflected in activities such as regular risk assessments, safety inspections, incident investigations, and management reviews to continuously identify weaknesses in management and take corrective and preventive actions to achieve a spiral-up of safety performance.
4. Context of the Organization
4.1 Understanding the organization and its context

The Country Organization shall determine external and internal issues that are relevant to its purpose and that affect its ability to achieve the intended outcome(s) of its OH&S management system. The Country Organization shall periodically monitor and review these internal and external environmental factors, which may affect the ability of the Country's projects to achieve the intended OHS outcomes.

An understanding of the context of the Country Organization is used to establish, implement, maintain and continually improve its OH&S management system. Internal and external issues can be positive or negative and include conditions, characteristics or changing circumstances that can affect the OH&S management system, for example:
a) external issues, such as:
the cultural, social, political, legal, financial, technological, economic and natural surroundings and market competition, whether international, national, regional or local;
introduction of new competitors, contractors, subcontractors, suppliers, partners and providers, new technologies, new laws and the emergence of new occupations;
new knowledge on products and their effect on health and safety;
key drivers and trends relevant to the industry or sector having impact on the organization;
relationships with, as well as perceptions and values of, its
external interested parties;
changes in relation to any of the above;
b) internal issues, such as:
governance, organizational structure, roles and accountabilities;
policies, objectives and the strategies that are in place to achieve them;
the capabilities, understood in terms of resources, knowledge and competence (e.g. capital, time, human resources, processes, systems and technologies);
information systems, information flows and decision-making processes (both formal and informal);
introduction of new products, materials, services, tools, software, premises and equipment;
relationships with, as well as perceptions and values of, workers;
the culture in the organization;
standards, guidelines and models adopted by the organization;
the form and extent of contractual relationships, including, for example, outsourced activities;
working time arrangements;
working conditions;
changes in relation to any of the above.

4.2 Understanding the needs and expectations of workers and other interested parties
The Country Organization shall determine:
the other interested parties, in addition to workers, that are relevant to the OH&S management system;
the relevant needs and expectations (i.e. requirements) of workers and other interested parties;
which of these needs and expectations are, or could become, legal requirements and other requirements.
Interested parties may have requirements related to climate change. Interested parties, in addition to workers, can include:
legal and regulatory authorities (local, regional, state/provincial, national or international);
parent organizations;
suppliers, contractors and subcontractors;
workers' representatives;
workers' organizations (trade unions) and employers' organizations;
owners, shareholders, clients, visitors, local community and neighbours of the organization and the general public;
medical and other community services, media, academia, business associations and non-governmental organizations (NGOs);
occupational health and safety organizations, occupational safety and health-care professionals.

Some needs and expectations are mandatory; for example, because they have been incorporated into laws and regulations. The Country Organization may also decide to voluntarily agree to, or adopt, other needs and expectations (e.g. subscribing to a voluntary initiative).
Once the Country Organization adopts them, they are addressed when planning and establishing the OH&S management system.

4.3 Determining the scope of the OH&S management system
The Country Organization has determined the boundaries and applicability of the OH&S management system to establish its scope.
When determining this scope, the organization shall:
consider the external and internal issues referred to in 4.1;
take into account the requirements referred to in 4.2;
take into account the planned or performed work-related activities.
The OH&S management system shall include the activities, products and services within the Country Organization's control or influence that can impact the Country Organization's OH&S performance.
The scope is described in Section 1.2 of this manual.
4.4 OHS management system

The Country Organization has established, implemented, maintained and continually improved an OHSMS, including the processes needed and their interactions, in accordance with the requirements of ISO 45001:2018. This is outlined in this manual (see Figure 1 - Relationship between PDCA and the 45001 standard model in Section 1.6). The Country Organization has established OHS system documents in accordance with the requirements of ISO 45001:2018 (see "Appendix 2: OHS Management System Elements and Supporting Documents Matrix").
5. Leadership and Worker Participation
5.1 Leadership and commitment
5.1.1The Country Organization's Top Management shall demonstrate leadership and commitment with respect to the OH&S management system by:
a) taking overall responsibility and accountability for the prevention of work-related injury and ill health, as well as the provision of safe and healthy workplaces and activities;
b) ensuring that the OH&S policy and related OH&S objectives are established and are compatible with the strategic direction of the Group;
c) ensuring the integration of the OH&S management system requirements into the Country Organization's business processes;
d) ensuring that the resources needed to establish, implement, maintain and improve the OH&S management system are available;
e) communicating the importance of effective OH&S management and of conforming to the OH&S management system requirements;
f) ensuring that the OH&S management system achieves its intended outcome(s);
g) directing and supporting persons to contribute to the effectiveness of the OH&S management system;
h) ensuring and promoting continual improvement;
i) supporting other relevant management roles to demonstrate their leadership as it applies to their areas of responsibility;
developing, leading and promoting a culture in the organization that supports the intended outcomes of the OH&S management system;
protecting workers from reprisals when reporting incidents, hazards, risks and opportunities;
ensuring the organization establishes and implements a process(es) for consultation and participation of workers (see 5.4);
m) supporting the establishment and functioning of health and safety committees.
5.1.2Safety Culture Development

The Country Organization's Top Management shall implement the "people-oriented, life first" safety concept, ensure the health and safety of employees, and establish core safety production values centered on respecting life, safety first, continual improvement, and pursuing excellence.

The Country Organization's Top Management shall fully consider internal and external cultural characteristics, plan and establish safety culture concepts recognized by all staff, organize and implement safety culture development, cultivate good safety behaviors, and create an excellent safety culture atmosphere.

5.2 OHS policy

The Country Organization's Top Management shall establish, implement and maintain an OH&S policy that: a) includes a commitment to provide safe and healthy working conditions for the prevention of work-related injury and ill health and is appropriate to the purpose, size and context of the organization and to the specific nature of its OH&S risks and OH&S opportunities; b) provides a framework for setting the OH&S objectives; c) includes a commitment to fulfil legal requirements and other requirements; d) includes a commitment to eliminate hazards and reduce OH&S risks (see 8.1.2); e) includes a commitment to continual improvement of the OH&S management system; f) includes a commitment to consultation and participation of workers, and, where they exist, workers' representatives. The OH&S policy shall: -beavailable as documented information; -becommunicated within the organization; -beavailable to interested parties, as appropriate; -berelevant and appropriate. The Country Organization's OHS policy is detailed in Section 3.0

"Occupational Health and Safety Policy" of this manual. The OHS policy is signed by the Country Organization's Top Management, clarifying the overall OHS policy statement and safety policy. All employees shall ensure it is understood, implemented, and maintained. All project departments of the Country Organization shall communicate it to all employees through training, the company intranet, and project notice boards. This policy and statement are available to interested parties upon request. The policy shall be reviewed periodically by the Country Organization's Top Management. Additionally, a comprehensive review shall be conducted annually, and reviews shall be conducted at any time when applicable regulations or interested parties' needs and expectations change, or when the nature of the Country Organization's business or main OHS risks change. Worker participation shall be included in the review of the OHS policy.
5.3 Organizational roles, responsibilities and authorities

The Country Organization's Top Management shall ensure that the responsibilities and authorities for relevant roles within the OH&S management system are assigned and communicated at all levels within the Country Organization and maintained as documented information. Workers at each level of the Country Organization shall assume responsibility for those aspects of the OH&S management system over which they have control. The Country Organization shall assign the responsibility and authority for: a) ensuring that the OH&S management system conforms to the requirements of the ISO 45001:2018 standard; b) reporting on the performance of the OH&S management system to top management. 5.3.1The Country Organization's Top Management shall determine and assign safety roles, responsibilities, and authorities for workers. The Country Organization's Top Management shall organize the establishment of bodies such as the Project Safety and Health Committee. Worker roles, responsibilities, and authorities are defined in OHSPS-PA-003 'Job Responsibilities and Authorities' and related procedural documents. 5.3.2The person in charge of each project department shall ensure that their project's OHS management system conforms to the requirements of the ISO 45001:2018 standard and shall report on the performance of the OHS management system to the Country Organization's Top Management
periodically.

5.4 Consultation and participation

The Country Organization shall establish, implement and maintain OHSPSPA-004 'Worker Consultation and Participation Procedure' for the consultation and participation of workers at all applicable levels and functions, and, where they exist, workers' representatives, in the development, planning, implementation, performance evaluation and actions for improvement of the OH&S management system.
The Country Organization shall:
provide mechanisms, time, training and resources necessary for consultation and participation;
provide timely access to clear, understandable and relevant information about the OH&S management system;
determine and remove obstacles or barriers to participation and minimize those that cannot be removed.
emphasize the consultation of non-managerial workers on the following:
determining the needs and expectations of interested parties (see 4.2);
establishing the OH&S policy (see 5.2);
assigning organizational roles, responsibilities and authorities, as applicable (see 5.3);
determining how to fulfil legal requirements and other requirements (see 6.1.3);
establishing OH&S objectives and planning to achieve them (see 6.2);
determining applicable controls for outsourcing, procurement and contractors (see 8.1.4);
determining what needs to be monitored, measured and evaluated (see 9.1);
planning, establishing, implementing and maintaining an audit programme(s) (see 9.2.2);
ensuring continual improvement (see 10.3);
emphasize the participation of non-managerial workers in the following:
determining the mechanisms for their consultation and participation;
identifying hazards and assessing risks and opportunities (see 6.1.1 and 6.1.2);
determining actions to eliminate hazards and reduce OH&S risks (see 6.1.4);
determining competence requirements, training needs, training and evaluating training (see 7.2);
determining what needs to be communicated and how this will be done (see 7.4);
determining control measures and their effective implementation and use (see 8.1, 8.1.3 and 8.2);
investigating incidents and nonconformities and determining corrective actions (see 10.2).

6. Planning
6.1 Actions to address risks and opportunities
6.1.1 General

When planning for the OH&S management system, the Country Organization has considered the issues referred to in 4.1 (context), the requirements referred to in 4.2 (interested parties) and 4.3 (the scope of its OH&S management system) and determined the risks and opportunities that need to be addressed to:
a) give assurance that the OH&S management system can achieve its intended outcome(s);
b) prevent, or reduce, undesired effects; c) achieve continual improvement.
When determining the risks and opportunities for the OH&S management system and its intended outcomes that need to be addressed, the Country Organization shall take into account:
-hazards (see 6.1.2.1); -OH&Srisks and other risks (see 6.1.2.2); -OH&Sopportunities and other opportunities (see 6.1.2.3); -legal requirements and other requirements (see 6.1.3).

The Country Organization, in its planning process(es), shall determine and assess the risks and opportunities that are relevant to the intended outcomes of the OH&S management system associated with changes in the organization, its processes or the OH&S management system.
